say: Chapter 1. The Refusal.
⟦muawiya⟧ died in Rajab 60 A H and his son ⟦yazid⟧ succeeded him, against the terms of the peace ⟦muawiya⟧ had made with Imam al-Hasan, peace be upon him.

⟦yazid⟧ wrote at once to al-Walid ⟦ibn⟧ Utba, governor of Medina, ordering him to take the oath of allegiance from ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, Abdullah ⟦ibn⟧ Umar and Abdullah ⟦ibn⟧ al-Zubayr, forcefully and without delay.
Some reports add that he ordered ⟦hussain⟧ killed if he refused.
Think about it. What would you do if someone powerful demanded that you support something wrong?
Rather than pledge allegiance to ⟦yazid⟧, ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, left Medina by night on 28 Rajab, after bidding farewell at the grave of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family.

With him went his household, among them his sister ⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧, peace be upon her, his brother ⟦abbas⟧, peace be upon him, and his son Ali (later Imam ⟦abidin⟧, peace be upon him), and a small group of companions.
Imam ⟦hussain⟧ said, to the governor of Medina: "A man like me does not pledge allegiance to a man like him."
Chapter 2. Refuge in Mecca.
The caravan reached Mecca on 3 Shaabaan and stayed for about four months.
The sanctuary offered protection, and pilgrims and visitors came to meet ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, and hear from him.
From ⟦kufa⟧ came a flood of letters, reportedly around 12,000, urging ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, to come and lead them.
⟦kufa⟧ had been the capital of his father, Imam Ali, peace be upon him, and many there resented Umayyad rule.
One letter, signed by Shabath ⟦ibn⟧ Ribi, Hajjar ⟦ibn⟧ Abjar, Amr ⟦ibn⟧ al-Hajjaj and others, promised "an army mustered for you"; the same men would later lead troops against him at ⟦karbala⟧.
One of the letters read: "The land has turned green, the fruits are ripe and the wells are full. Come, if you wish, to an army mustered for you."
Think about it. If you promise to help someone, what makes that promise real?
⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, sent his cousin Muslim ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦aqil⟧, peace be upon him, to ⟦kufa⟧, by way of Medina, to test the people's sincerity.
The welcome was overwhelming: some 18,000 people pledged their support, and Muslim, peace be upon him, wrote urging ⟦hussain⟧ to come.
On 8 Dhul Hijja, the day pilgrims set out for Mina, ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, left Mecca.
He had learned of a plan to assassinate him inside the sanctuary and would not let its sanctity be broken by his blood.
He completed an Umra in place of the Hajj and set out for Iraq.
Think about it. Why is the caravan going the opposite way from everyone else?
Chapter 3. The Road North.
At al-Saffah the caravan met the poet al-⟦farazdaq⟧, travelling from Iraq.
⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, asked him what he had seen of the people there.
al-⟦farazdaq⟧ said: "Their hearts are with you, but their swords are with Banu Umayya."
The new governor, ⟦ubaydullah⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦ziyad⟧, took control of ⟦kufa⟧ with threats and bribes.
The thousands who had pledged to Muslim, peace be upon him, melted away until he stood alone.
He was captured and killed, with his host Hani ⟦ibn⟧ Urwa, on 9 Dhul Hijja: one day after ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, left Mecca.
Near ⟦zarud⟧ and ⟦thalabiyya⟧, travellers from ⟦kufa⟧ brought news of the deaths of Muslim, peace be upon him, and Hani.
⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, recited "To God we belong, and to Him we return."
Around this time ⟦zuhayr⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦qayn⟧, who had been avoiding the caravan, was invited to meet ⟦hussain⟧.
He came back from the meeting changed, sent his wife home to her family, and joined him.
At ⟦zubala⟧ word came that another messenger, Abdullah ⟦ibn⟧ Yaqtur, had been killed.
⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, spoke openly: "Our supporters have abandoned us. Whoever of you wishes to leave may go; he owes us nothing."
Many who had joined on the road expecting an easy victory left.
Those who had come with him from Medina stayed.
Think about it. Why would Imam ⟦hussain⟧ tell everyone the truth, knowing that people would leave?
Chapter 4. Meeting ⟦hurr⟧.
Near Sharaf, about 1,000 horsemen appeared: the vanguard of ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦ziyad⟧'s forces under al-⟦hurr⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦yazid⟧ al-Riyahi.
Their orders were to stop ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, from turning back and to bring him to ⟦kufa⟧.
⟦hurr⟧'s men and horses arrived parched in the midday heat.
⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, who had ordered extra water drawn at Sharaf that morning, told his companions to water them all, men and horses alike.
Days later at ⟦karbala⟧, the army ⟦hurr⟧ served would cut ⟦hussain⟧'s camp off from the river.
Think about it. Why would Imam ⟦hussain⟧ give water to an army sent to stop him?
When the time of the noon prayer came, ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, had the adhan called and asked ⟦hurr⟧ whether he would lead his own men.
⟦hurr⟧ replied that they would pray behind ⟦hussain⟧.
Afterwards ⟦hussain⟧ addressed them and produced saddlebags full of the letters ⟦kufa⟧ had sent.
⟦hurr⟧ answered that he was not one of those who had written.
Think about it. The soldiers prayed behind Imam ⟦hussain⟧, yet still obeyed orders against him. Why might that be?

⟦hurr⟧ would neither let ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, return to Medina nor take him into ⟦kufa⟧, so they agreed on a road that led to neither, and the caravan moved north-west with ⟦hurr⟧'s horsemen alongside.
At al-Baydha ⟦hussain⟧ addressed ⟦hurr⟧'s men, reminding them of the Prophet's words about those who stay silent before a tyrant.
Near Qasr Bani Muqatil he woke from a short rest reciting "To God we belong and to Him we return".
His son ⟦akbar⟧, peace be upon him, asked, "Are we not in the right?"
When he answered yes, ⟦akbar⟧ said: "Then we do not mind if we die in the right."
Chapter 5. ⟦karbala⟧.
On 2 ⟦muharram⟧ 61 A H the caravan halted on a plain west of the Euphrates.
⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, asked its name and was told ⟦karbala⟧.
He said it was a land of karb (anguish) and balaa (trial): here their mounts would kneel, and here their blood would be shed.
The tents were pitched.
Umar ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦saad⟧ arrived with 4,000 men, and reinforcements swelled his army to many thousands; reports range as high as 30,000.
On 7 ⟦muharram⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦ziyad⟧ ordered the water cut off, and 500 horsemen under Amr ⟦ibn⟧ al-Hajjaj took the banks of the Euphrates.
For three days the camp, children included, went without water.
On the 9th the army advanced, and ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, asked for one more night, to spend in prayer.
Think of the last time you were really thirsty. Now imagine three days in the desert heat.
On the eve of ⟦ashura⟧, ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, gathered his companions, thanked them, and released them from their pledge: the enemy wanted only him.
He had the lamps put out so that anyone could slip away unseen.
None did.
They spent the night in prayer and reciting the Quran; it is said their voices hummed through the camp like bees.
Think about it. What does loyalty mean to you?
Chapter 6. ⟦ashura⟧.
At dawn on 10 ⟦muharram⟧ the army of Umar ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦saad⟧ drew up in its ranks.
al-⟦hurr⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦yazid⟧, trembling, edged his horse away from them and rode to ⟦hussain⟧'s camp, asking whether his repentance could be accepted.
⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, rode out to him and welcomed him.
⟦hurr⟧ was among the first of the companions to fall that day.
Imam ⟦hussain⟧ said, to ⟦hurr⟧: "You are al-⟦hurr⟧, free, as your mother named you: free in this world and in the Hereafter."
Think about it. Is it ever too late to change your mind and do what is right?
Through 10 ⟦muharram⟧ the companions went out one by one, and after them the men of the Prophet's family.
At noon ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, led the prayer in the open while ⟦said⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ Abdullah al-Hanafi shielded him with his own body.
⟦abbas⟧, peace be upon him, fell by the river, trying to bring water for the children.
By the time of Asr, ⟦hussain⟧ stood alone.
al-⟦hurr⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦yazid⟧ al-Riyahi. The commander who changed sides that morning.
Burayr ⟦ibn⟧ Khudayr. A reciter and teacher of the Quran from ⟦kufa⟧.
Wahb ⟦ibn⟧ Abdullah al-Kalbi. A young man who came with his mother and his wife.
Muslim ⟦ibn⟧ Awsaja. An old companion, loyal to his last breath.
Abu Thumama al-Saidi. He reminded the Imam that it was time for the noon prayer.
⟦said⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ Abdullah al-Hanafi. He shielded the Imam with his body during the prayer.
Habib ⟦ibn⟧ Muzahir. An elderly companion of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and of Imam Ali, peace be upon him.
⟦zuhayr⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦qayn⟧. He had joined the caravan on the road.
Nafi ⟦ibn⟧ Hilal. An archer who wrote his name on his arrows.
Abis ⟦ibn⟧ Abi Shabib al-Shakiri. A devoted Kufan who had come with Muslim's letter.
Jawn. An elderly African freedman of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari.
⟦akbar⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ al-⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him. The Imam's eldest son, who most resembled the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family.
Abdullah ⟦ibn⟧ Muslim ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦aqil⟧, peace be upon him. Son of Muslim ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦aqil⟧, the envoy to ⟦kufa⟧.
Awn and Muhammad, peace be upon them. The sons of ⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧, peace be upon her.
⟦qasim⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ al-Hasan, peace be upon him. Son of Imam al-Hasan, peace be upon him, still a teenager.
⟦abbas⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ Ali, peace be upon him. The standard-bearer, who went to the river for water for the children.
Abdullah, the infant, peace be upon him. The Imam's baby son, also called Ali al-Asghar, peace be upon him.
Imam al-⟦hussain⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ Ali, peace be upon him. Grandson of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family. At the time of Asr.
As the Quran says: "Do not think of those killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord."
Think about it. Choose one of these names. What would you like to find out about them?

At the time of Asr on 10 ⟦muharram⟧ 61 A H, ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, grandson of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, was killed, thirsty, on the plain of ⟦karbala⟧, having refused to the last to give his hand to ⟦yazid⟧.
His horse, remembered as ⟦zuljanah⟧, returned to the tents without its rider, and the women knew what had happened.
Imam ⟦hussain⟧ said, on the road to ⟦karbala⟧: "I see death as nothing but happiness, and life with oppressors as nothing but misery."
Chapter 7. The Captives' Journey.
On the evening of ⟦ashura⟧ the camp was plundered and the tents set alight.
The surviving women and children, with the gravely ill Ali ⟦ibn⟧ al-⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, Imam ⟦abidin⟧, spent the night in the open.
⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧, peace be upon her, kept watch over them until dawn; it is said that from exhaustion she offered her night prayer sitting down.
The night is remembered as Shaam-e Ghareebaan, the evening of the strangers.

On 12 ⟦muharram⟧ the captives, the women and children of the Prophet's family and the ailing Imam ⟦abidin⟧, peace be upon him, were brought into ⟦kufa⟧, the city whose letters had invited ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him.
In the streets ⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧, peace be upon her, rebuked the weeping Kufans for their broken promises.
In his palace ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦ziyad⟧ taunted her, asking how she saw what God had done to her brother.
She replied: "I saw nothing but beauty."
As the captives were led through ⟦kufa⟧, crowds gathered and many wept.
⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧, peace be upon her, signalled for silence and addressed them; those who heard her said it was as if Ali, peace be upon him, himself were speaking.
She rebuked the Kufans for inviting ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, and then abandoning him, and told them their tears could not wash away what they had done.
⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧ said:
O people of ⟦kufa⟧, people of deceit and betrayal: do you weep? May your tears never dry.
You are like the woman who unravels her yarn after she has spun it strong.
So weep much, and laugh little.
Do you know whose heart, so dear to the Messenger of God, you have torn apart?
After a long march through Iraq and Syria, the captives were brought into Damascus around 1 Safar 61 A H.
Some reports describe the city decorated as if for a celebration, and many in the crowds did not know who the captives were.
They were led to the palace of ⟦yazid⟧.
In his court ⟦yazid⟧ mocked the captives and celebrated his victory.
⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧, peace be upon her, rose and answered him, opening with a verse of the Quran (30:10) and declaring that his power was fleeting and his crime would be remembered forever.
Imam ⟦abidin⟧, peace be upon him, later spoke in the mosque of Damascus, telling the people who the captives really were.
Their words turned the court's triumph into shame, and the story of ⟦karbala⟧ began to spread.
Standing before ⟦yazid⟧, ⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧ said:
Then the end of those who did evil was the worst of ends, for they denied the signs of God.
Do you think, ⟦yazid⟧, that because we are led as captives we are lowly before God, and you are honoured by Him?
So plot your plots, strive your utmost, spare no effort:
by God, you will never erase our remembrance, nor kill our revelation.
Is your judgement anything but folly, your days anything but numbered, your gathering anything but scattered?
Think about it. How can words be stronger than an army?

On 20 Safar 61 A H, forty days after ⟦ashura⟧, ⟦jabir⟧ ⟦ibn⟧ Abdullah al-Ansari, an elderly companion of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, who had lost his sight, reached ⟦karbala⟧ with Atiyya al-Awfi and visited the grave of ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him:
the first pilgrim of ⟦arbaeen⟧.
Many reports say the family, returning from Damascus, came to ⟦karbala⟧ that same day before going on to Medina.
Today ⟦arbaeen⟧ draws millions of pilgrims on foot.
Think about it. Why do you think millions still walk to ⟦karbala⟧ today?

Imam ⟦hussain⟧, peace be upon him, ⟦abbas⟧, peace be upon him, and ⟦sayyida⟧ ⟦zaynab⟧, peace be upon her, travelled from Medina to ⟦karbala⟧, while ⟦yazid⟧ ruled from Damascus and ⟦ibn⟧ ⟦ziyad⟧ from ⟦kufa⟧.
